Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: A grandchild brings up a general question about navigating a new phase of their life.
Situation2: This is the last weekend before the partner relocates abroad for months.
Story: I sat at the kitchen table, my phone buzzing with a message from my partner: “Can’t wait for our weekend together. Just us.” My heart fluttered, knowing this was our last chance to be close before he left for months. I wanted to savor every moment, to make memories that would carry us through the distance. Just as I was about to reply, my granddaughter walked in, her eyes uncertain. “Grandma, can I talk to you? I’m not sure what to do about college and friends. Everything’s changing so fast.” She looked at me, searching for the wisdom she believed I held. I felt the weight of her trust, the expectation to guide her through this confusing time. But my mind was torn—my partner needed me, too. I could almost hear the clock ticking, each second pulling me in two directions. My chest tightened as I tried to smile at my granddaughter, my phone still glowing with my partner’s message. I wanted to be everything for both of them, but I could already feel myself stretching thin, caught between love and responsibility, unsure which path to take.
